title: FAQ

**Q: Is desmobil.com's login broken right now?**
A: No -- private customer registration and login work. Only dealer/business registration is blocked, and only until the SQL in section 4 is run.

**Q: Did any real customer data get exposed?**
A: Two real customers (registered 2026-07-15) had a BOP-console identity row silently created for them (role: viewer), which is the field the console uses to authorize sessions. Those two rows were removed; their actual desmobil accounts were untouched. No evidence either logged into the console.

**Q: Why couldn't the SQL trigger just be fixed automatically?**
A: DDL (DROP TRIGGER/FUNCTION) isn't exposed via the Supabase REST API, and no direct Postgres connection string or Supabase CLI link exists on the VPS -- it requires the Supabase Dashboard SQL Editor, which needs your own authenticated session.

**Q: Is dealer_verified actually enforced anywhere yet?**
A: It's server-enforced against self-declaration (client can never set it true) and triggers an admin email on every business signup. No BOP-side dealer approval UI exists yet -- that would be a natural next step once you decide what a verified dealer should actually receive.

title: Why is a lead red?
body_md: The lead has been in `new`/`reviewing` for more than **2 hours** — the public promise on desmobil.com is an offer within 2 business hours. Red leads are breaching it.

title: Where do leads come from?
body_md: The `/sell` wizard on desmobil.com (source `web`). WhatsApp and phone leads can be entered later with source `whatsapp`/`phone`. Junk is filtered by honeypot + rate limit (5/h per IP).

title: Sell Leads — acquisition funnel inbox
body_md: Inbox for the desmobil.com **Sell Vehicle** funnel (Phase 1 instant offer). Each row is a seller who submitted their vehicle — DES is the buyer. The **SLA badge** shows elapsed time while a lead is `new` or `reviewing`; it turns red past the promised **2 business hours**. Revenue comes from trade-to-retail margin, so response speed is the whole game.

title: Part of flow: Sell Acquisition (Inkoop)
body_md:
This screen is a step in the **Sell Acquisition (Inkoop)** business flow (`process:sell-acquisition`).

**Chain:** desmobil `/sell` wizard → `sell_leads` → **SA013** triage → **SA014** offer & negotiation → `purchased` → listing creation in **MP001/MP003**.

This screen's step: **Triage (SA013):** work red SLA badges first — the 2-hour promise is the differentiator. Open the lead.

title: Vehicle types
body_md: Six seller-facing types: van, truck, commercial_truck, camper, **car**, **caravan** (+ boat reserved). RDW heuristic pre-selects: Bedrijfsauto ≤3.5t → van, >3.5t → truck, opleggertrekker → commercial, kampeer → camper, Personenauto → car, caravan trailer → caravan. Taxonomy mapping on submit: van 1000, truck/commercial 2000, car 3000, camper 4000, caravan 5000.

title: Work a new lead
body_md:
1. Open the red/oldest SLA leads first.
2. Click the row to open the lead detail (SA014).
3. Review vehicle, five answers and photos; set a valuation range.
4. Enter `our_offer_eur` and press **Send offer email** — the lead moves to `offer_sent` automatically.

title: Why can I not send the offer?
body_md: **Our offer (€)** must be filled first, and SMTP must be configured. The button is disabled otherwise.

title: Sell Lead Detail — evaluate and make the offer
body_md: Full view of one acquisition lead: vehicle card (RDW data if the seller used a Dutch plate), the **five questions** (mileage, condition, damage, BTW status, finance), seller contact with **Call / WhatsApp / Email** buttons, photo gallery (signed URLs from the private `sell-leads` bucket), valuation & offer fields, the status machine, internal notes and the event timeline.

title: Part of flow: Sell Acquisition (Inkoop)
body_md:
This screen is a step in the **Sell Acquisition (Inkoop)** business flow (`process:sell-acquisition`).

**Chain:** desmobil `/sell` wizard → `sell_leads` → **SA013** triage → **SA014** offer & negotiation → `purchased` → listing creation in **MP001/MP003**.

This screen's step: **Evaluate (SA014):** review vehicle/RDW data, five answers, photos. Set internal valuation low/high.

title: Data sources
body_md: Tables: `sell_leads`, `sell_lead_images`, `sell_lead_events`. RDW raw responses are stored in `rdw_data` (jsonb). Photos: private bucket `sell-leads`, EXIF/GPS stripped at ingest.

title: Send an offer
body_md:
1. Fill **Valuation low/high** (internal only, never shown to the seller).
2. Enter **Our offer (€)**.
3. Press **Send offer email** — template C goes to the seller in their language (NL/EN authored; others fall back to EN), valid 7 days, and the status moves to `offer_sent`.
4. Every send is logged to the timeline (`offer_sent`, `email_sent`).

title: Status machine
body_md: `new → reviewing → offer_sent → negotiating → accepted → purchased`, with exits `declined_by_us`, `rejected_by_seller`, `expired`, `lost`. Only valid transitions are offered as buttons; every change is written to `sell_lead_events`.

title: What does a red ⚠ flag on a message mean?
body_md: The first message of a thread contained a URL or phone number — the classic marketplace-scam pattern. Treat with care; block if clearly spam.

title: Buyer Inbox — desmobil buyer conversations
body_md: On-platform messaging between desmobil.com buyers and DES. One conversation per **buyer × listing** — the buyer's email is never exposed until you choose to use it. Unread threads sort first with an orange counter. Buyers write from their account (verified email required); you reply here as DESMOBIL.

title: Part of flow: Buyer Messaging & Offers
body_md:
This screen is a step in the **Buyer Messaging & Offers** business flow (`process:buyer-messaging`).

**Chain:** desmobil listing → **Contact Seller** (login required) → `dm_conversations` (one thread per buyer × listing) → **SA015** inbox → **SA016** reply → offer messages mirror into `crm_leads` (**CR001**).

title: Part of flow: DESMOBIL Account Journey
body_md:
This screen is a step in the **DESMOBIL Account Journey** business flow (`process:dm-account-journey`).

**Chain:** anonymous favorites (localStorage) → magic-link/Google login (`dm_profiles` trigger) → favorites/recent-views **merge** → saved searches + hourly alert cron → conversations → console **SA015/SA016**.

This screen's step: **Engagement:** Contact Seller / Make Offer require the account — feeding the Buyer Messaging flow (SA015/SA016).

title: Handle a new message
body_md:
1. Open the thread (unread counter clears).
2. Reply — the buyer gets an email notification with a **deep link back to desmobil.com** (message content is never sent by email).
3. Offers arrive as structured messages and also create a `crm_leads` row with `expected_value`.
4. Use **Close** when a conversation ends, **Block** for abuse.

title: Does replying email the buyer?
body_md: Yes — a notification email with a link to their desmobil account inbox. The message text itself stays on-platform so conversations remain auditable.

title: Buyer Thread — reply, verify, decide
body_md: Single conversation view: chat history (buyer left, DES orange right), buyer contact card and thread controls. Business buyers show a verification badge: amber **BUSINESS — UNVERIFIED** or green **✓ VERIFIED DEALER**.

title: When should I NOT force-release?
body_md: When the holder is actively editing — they would lose the lock mid-edit and a second editor could cause lost updates. The version column on `bop_listings` is the last safety net, not a replacement for locking.

title: Lock Monitor — SAP SM12-style object locks
body_md: Shows all active rows in `bop_object_locks` (Object Lock Service). Any console session editing a listing takes an **exclusive lock** (atomic upsert — race-free); others see a read-only banner. Locks heartbeat every 60s and expire after 4 minutes without one, so crashes self-heal.

title: Force-release a lock
body_md:
1. Find the row (object, holder, age, heartbeat staleness).
2. Press force-release and confirm — use only when the holder is genuinely gone; the release is audited.
3. Stale locks (expired heartbeat) can be released safely at any time.

body_md: Primary tables: `wrk_inspections`, `wrk_orders`, `wrk_labour_rates` (Supabase/Postgres). This screen writes — inspection results are saved per work order. Rates are read-only for cost estimation.

title: APIs & data
body_md:
- `/api/bop/wrk/inspections` — GET/POST/PATCH → `wrk_inspections`
- `/api/bop/wrk/orders` — GET → `wrk_orders` (linked WO context)
- `/api/bop/wrk/rates` — GET → `wrk_labour_rates` (cost lookup)

title: APK Reminders
body_md:
**APK Reminders** (`WK006`) belongs to the Workshop Intelligence module. Route: `/console/wrk/apk-reminders`.

Manages the Dutch APK (Algemene Periodieke Keuring) inspection reminder campaign. Tracks vehicle APK expiry dates, sends reminders to customers, and converts reminders into work orders.

title: Where does this data live?
body_md: Primary tables: `wrk_apk_reminders` (Supabase/Postgres). This screen writes — reminder records are created and updated as campaigns run and customers respond.

title: APIs & data
body_md: - `/api/bop/wrk/apk-reminders` — GET/POST/PATCH → `wrk_apk_reminders`

title: Customer Approvals
body_md:
**Customer Approvals** (`WK007`) belongs to the Workshop Intelligence module. Route: `/console/wrk/approvals`.

Tracks additional work items that require customer approval before proceeding. Items come from inspections (WK005) or technician recommendations. Shows approval status and links back to the parent work order.

title: Where does this data live?
body_md: Primary tables: `wrk_approvals`, `wrk_orders` (Supabase/Postgres). This screen writes — approval records are created from inspections and updated when the customer responds.

title: APIs & data
body_md:
- `/api/bop/wrk/approvals` — GET/POST/PATCH → `wrk_approvals`
- `/api/bop/wrk/orders` — GET → `wrk_orders` (parent WO context)

title: Customer Status
body_md:
**Customer Status** (`WK008`) belongs to the Workshop Intelligence module. Route: `/console/wrk/status`.

Customer-facing work order status tracker. Shows the current stage of each vehicle in the workshop — useful for front-desk staff and customer-facing status pages.

title: Where does this data live?
body_md: Primary tables: `wrk_orders` (Supabase/Postgres). This screen is read-only — it reads work order status and presents a simplified customer view.

title: APIs & data
body_md: - `/api/bop/wrk/status` — GET → `wrk_orders`

title: Daily Briefing
body_md:
**Daily Briefing** (`WK009`) belongs to the Workshop Intelligence module. Route: `/console/wrk/briefing`.

Morning briefing view for workshop managers: today's planned work orders, technician availability, pending APK reminders, and any carryover from yesterday. Designed for a quick stand-up review.

title: Where does this data live?
body_md: Primary tables: `wrk_orders`, `wrk_planning_slots`, `wrk_technicians`, `wrk_apk_reminders` (Supabase/Postgres). This screen is read-only — it aggregates today's schedule and outstanding items.

title: APIs & data
body_md: - `/api/bop/wrk/briefing` — GET → `wrk_orders`, `wrk_planning_slots`, `wrk_technicians`, `wrk_apk_reminders`

title: Repair Recommendations
body_md:
**Repair Recommendations** (`WK010`) belongs to the Workshop Intelligence module. Route: `/console/wrk/recommendations`.

AI-assisted repair and upsell recommendations based on vehicle history, mileage, inspection results, and service intervals. Helps technicians identify additional work that adds value for the customer.

title: Where does this data live?
body_md: Primary tables: `wrk_orders`, `wrk_planning_slots`, `wrk_technicians`, `wrk_efficiency_metrics`, `wrk_apk_reminders` (Supabase/Postgres). This screen is read-only — it analyses existing data to generate recommendations.

title: APIs & data
body_md: - `/api/bop/wrk/recommendations` — GET → `wrk_orders`, `wrk_planning_slots`, `wrk_technicians`, `wrk_efficiency_metrics`, `wrk_apk_reminders`

title: Labour Rates
body_md:
**Labour Rates** (`WK011`) belongs to the Workshop Intelligence module. Route: `/console/wrk/rates`.

Manage hourly labour rates by work type (mechanical, electrical, bodywork, diagnostic, etc.). Rates are used by work orders and inspections for cost calculations.

title: Where does this data live?
body_md: Primary tables: `wrk_labour_rates` (Supabase/Postgres). This screen writes — rates are created and updated directly. Changes take effect on new work orders immediately.

title: APIs & data
body_md: - `/api/bop/wrk/rates` — GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE → `wrk_labour_rates`

title: Service Packages
body_md:
**Service Packages** (`WK012`) belongs to the Workshop Intelligence module. Route: `/console/wrk/packages`.

Define and manage predefined service packages (e.g. "Small Service", "APK + Service", "Winter Check"). Each package bundles labour lines and optional parts, making it easy to create consistent work orders.

title: Where does this data live?
body_md: Primary tables: `wrk_service_packages` (Supabase/Postgres). This screen writes — packages are created and edited directly. They are referenced when creating work orders.

title: APIs & data
body_md: - `/api/bop/wrk/packages` — GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE → `wrk_service_packages`

title: DMS Integration
body_md:
**DMS Integration** (`WK013`) belongs to the Workshop Intelligence module. Route: `/console/wrk/dms-integration`.

Autoflex DMS (Dealer Management System) integration hub. Configure API credentials, manage field mappings between BOP and Autoflex, trigger manual syncs, and monitor sync logs. Supports bi-directional data exchange for vehicles, customers, work orders, and parts.

title: Where does this data live?
body_md: Primary tables: `wrk_autoflex_config`, `wrk_autoflex_sync_logs`, `wrk_autoflex_field_maps`, `wrk_orders`, `ast_assets`, `crm_leads`, `shp_products` (Supabase/Postgres). This screen writes — configuration and field mappings are editable. Sync logs are read-only audit trails.

title: APIs & data
body_md:
- `/api/bop/wrk/autoflex` — GET/POST/PATCH → `wrk_autoflex_config`, `wrk_autoflex_sync_logs`, `wrk_orders`, `ast_assets`, `crm_leads`, `shp_products`
- `/api/bop/wrk/autoflex/logs` — GET → `wrk_autoflex_sync_logs`
